terms.gloss: a national song; the national anthem
terms.grammar: noun phrase: carmen, carminis n., with the adjective patrium
terms.comment: Curtius’s phrase, which Lewis & Short render “a national song”: the hymn the Persian Magi sang at the head of the king’s procession. Patrius here is “of one’s own country”, as in patrius sermō, one’s mother tongue (Cic. Fin. 1.4, Lewis & Short). Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for an anthem; using the phrase for one is our choice.

phrases.english: next came the Magi, singing their national hymn
They’re playing the national anthem; let’s stand up.

sources: Lewis & Short: carmen · Lewis & Short: patrius
